summary.headline: Q4 FY26 turnover rose 8.76% to INR1,322.30 crores but PAT fell 3.63% to INR80.14 crores; FY27 growth guided at 15-20%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 turnover grew 8.76% YoY to INR1,322.30 crores, while PAT declined 3.63% to INR80.14 crores and EBITDA margin compressed to 9.35% from 10.17%. For FY26, turnover rose 11.38% to INR4,565.20 crores and PAT rose 31.17% to INR264.32 crores, with EBITDA margin at 9.52% versus 8.34%. Management blamed Q4 on labour flight from NCR and Bengal/Assam elections, NGT construction bans, a cash crunch in Assam, and war-driven LPG, fuel and supply-chain disruption. The company guided to 15-20% revenue growth and double-digit EBITDA margin for FY27, with an order inflow target of about INR8,000 crores, but gave no formal PAT guidance.

segments.name: Central Vista (EPC, design-build, INR2,600-3,000 crores)
segments.commentary: Awarded 14 January 2026; Nirman Bhawan demolished and excavation/concrete started. Management targets about INR1,000 crores of FY27 execution, with a turnover run-rate of INR100-150 crores per month.

segments.name: CSMT Mumbai (order value INR2,076 crores ex-GST)
segments.commentary: Designs now approved and execution has picked up after a slow 1.5 years. FY27 execution target is about INR600 crores.

segments.name: Dahlias (private)
segments.commentary: FY27 execution target about INR400 crores.

segments.name: IJPM - India Jewellery Park (Mumbai)
segments.commentary: Design changes ongoing; ground work expected to start in the last month of Q1 FY27 after the Mumbai monsoon. FY27 target kept modest at about INR100 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20%, up from the 10-15% guidance given in prior years.
EBITDA margin expected to reach double digits in FY27 (currently 9.5% in FY26); management said margins will rise over the next two years as mechanisation takes effect.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR8,000 crores, including two L1 positions worth INR1,620.95 crores (RML Hospital Delhi and an Odisha government university project in Bhubaneswar).
FY27 capex about INR300 crores, down from an earlier guidance of about INR500 crores; FY26 capex was about INR274 crores.
Q1 FY27 expected to be very slow due to elections, labour exodus and Eid; ramp-up from Q2 and H2 significantly above H1.
Management said no guidance is prudent beyond FY27 given headwinds; a FY28 number was not given. Share buyback 'not in the offing'.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR274 crores; FY27 capex planned at about INR300 crores, with depreciation rising in line.

Mechanisation (tower cranes, passenger hoists costing INR50-70 lakh each, batching plants, concrete pumps) is the stated response to labour shortage. Management estimated the IRR uplift at 7-10% and payback at 4-5 years on equipment with a 4-year life; other assets have a 7-8 year life.
Q4 depreciation was about INR29 crores; management expects a similar run-rate going forward.
Management is evaluating precast and pre-engineered building technologies, but said these would take 2-3 years to be used on projects.
demand_pricing: Government vs private mix is targeted at roughly half and half. Private clients were over 60% of the order book, per an analyst's read.
Fixed-price orders are 11% of the order book; 89% of orders have built-in escalation clauses.
Government contracts use WPI-linked escalation with about a one-quarter lag; private contracts pass through volatile materials (cement, steel, grit, sand) roughly month-on-month.
Management is walking away from some projects, including with existing clients, and is raising bid margins by a couple of percentage points or more.
Pipeline has been slowed by the war, with developers delaying launches. The company is bidding selectively with existing or well-funded clients.
Competitors named: L&T, B&F, Nagarjuna, Shapoorji Pallonji, Kalpataru and Tata Projects.

qa_highlights.question: Will execution ramp up in FY27-28, and what growth should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth guided at 15-20% and order inflow target about INR8,000 crores. FY28 was not guided; management said FY28 is 'similar' and gave no firm number.

qa_highlights.question: Why are capex and depreciation rising while margins lag, and is this a new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the industry is at an inflection point due to labour shortage and taller, more complex buildings. Mechanisation benefits will take 2-3 years to show; FY27 capex is about INR300 crores, and depreciation is expected to grow in line.

qa_highlights.question: How are cost inflation and fuel-price increases being protected against?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost all contracts have escalation clauses; WPI-linked government recovery is lagging, and the company is seeking government compensation. Private contracts are pass-through for basic materials.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 margin fall was due to inflation vs. disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gross margin decline mainly to under-absorbed IDC and overheads from lost execution days, plus staff cost increments taken in January; inflation was a smaller factor, largely covered by escalation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fixed-price share, and how is margin protected in the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed-price orders are 11% of the order book. The 89% escalation-linked share and a better mix (private/public, geography) underpin the double-digit margin target.

qa_highlights.question: Are IJPM and the two L1 projects likely to convert?
qa_highlights.answer: RML Hospital (Delhi) and an Odisha university project are old tenders with no LOA date. Either side can rebid or cancel if escalation has moved too far.

risks_watch: Prolonged war: fuel, metal and LPG prices, supply-chain delays (electrical panels now 4+ months vs 2 earlier), and a possible rupee impact.
Labour shortage expected to persist for 3-4 years, with labour drawn from only 3-4 states; NGT construction bans in NCR add shutdown days.
Q1 FY27 expected to be very weak, so FY27 growth depends on a strong H2.
Receivables and working capital: working capital days at 104 (103 in the prior period); mobilisation advance INR802 crores, about 37% interest-bearing; retention INR450 crores.
Government WPI-linked escalation is lagging; management has lodged representations with the government.
Pipeline slowdown and possible cancellation or rebidding of the two L1 orders.
Shareholders pressing for a buyback; management declined, citing the need for a war chest. Net cash position is INR817 crores.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 growth and double-digit margins, with a strong order book and stable state governments cited. Cautious and evasive on FY28 guidance, the buyback and the link between capex and margins. Management repeatedly attributed Q4 weakness to labour and elections, and noted a prolonged war as the key risk.
key_quotes: We are giving a guidance of 15% to 20% in this year.
The margin profile, as I said in my last call I have given an indication of double digit and we are nearly there.
So at the moment, the share buyback is not in the offing. That's not even crossed our mind.
Labour shortage is here to stay.
